title: Strategy Pattern
concept: The Strategy pattern defines a family of algorithms, encapsulates each one, and makes them interchangeable — behavior selected at runtime via interfaces.
why: Hardcoding algorithm choices (sort type, compression, payment method) creates rigid code. Strategy lets you swap behavior without changing the code that uses it.
tips: Define the strategy interface first — it's the contract that all strategies must fulfill
Keep strategies stateless when possible — easier to reason about and test
Use Box[dyn Strategy] for runtime selection, generics for compile-time selection
Strategies should be SINGLE-RESPONSIBILITY — one algorithm per implementation
common_mistakes: Making strategies mutable — they should be pure functions, not stateful objects
Too many strategy variants — consider parameterizing one implementation instead of creating 10
Using strategy for trivial choices — a boolean flag or enum is sometimes simpler and clearer
